sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: hook h1, an incidental attribution against the company's own complete-looking account (playbook kind 2), with the newer guide's "second mention, different words": Doc 3's own impairment account (Asset Impairments section and table, three headline mentions of the $960 million BODYARMOR charge) omits the $1,274 million held-for-sale charge it books under Transaction Gains/Losses; only Doc 5's later wording ("the previously recorded impairment charge") classifies it. Target hard. Sentence and answer carried word for word from sketch i01 (origin claude, 2026-10-15). Local strong-solver screen on this exact sentence: 3/3 right, high confidence each (record in notes/sketches/i01.md; raw returns runs/i01-screen-5f5d5f5c3c208f15/returns.md; ledger row 38). User quick test against the High model 2026-10-15: survived ("i01, i02 all survived"). Platform difficulty result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 3 supplies both candidate amounts (1,274 under Transaction Gains/Losses, 960 under Asset Impairments) and dates both to the three months and year ended December 31, 2025; Doc 5 supplies the classification (its Q2 2026 reduction of 66 exceeds the Q1 2026 addition of 10 = 66 - 56, so the impairment charge being reduced includes the Q4 2025 charge); comparison 1,274 > 960.
- Universe: every 2025 charge any release calls an impairment or reduces as one: BODYARMOR 960 (Q4); LatAm trademark 31 (Q2) and 13 (Q4), FY 44; APAC trademark and PP&E 41 (Q4); LatAm equity-investee OTTI 40 (Q2); LatAm JV OTTI 25 (Q1); African bottling held for sale 1,274 (Q4, impairment per Doc 5). Charges never called impairments, all smaller than 960: Nigeria held for sale 393 (Q3), Ghana refranchising 36 (28 in Q2 "related to assets held for sale", 8 in Q3), fairlife remeasurement 47 (Q1), restructuring, transaction costs. Equity-investee items (proportionate share, FY 21) are not described as impairments.
- Necessity: D05 (Doc 3) is the only source of 1,274 and 960 (searched "1,274", "BODYARMOR", "held for sale", "impair" in all five; Docs 1, 2 and 5 carry only H1/9M 2025 items, Doc 4 only Q1 2025 and Q1 2026). D03 (Doc 5) is the only source naming the earlier charge an impairment ("previously recorded impairment charge"); Doc 4 (D01) calls the Q1 2026 addition "an impairment charge of $10 million related to our bottling operations in Africa" but does not point back to 2025 (screen solvers: "weaker alternative", "impairment only by analogy"), so it is not ticked or used in the reasoning. Delete-and-guess: without Doc 3, the largest 2025 impairment visible is the $40 million OTTI (Docs 1, 5): no gold; without Doc 5 (and Doc 4), a solver answers 960, the largest charge any 2025 release calls an impairment (all three screen solvers named 960 as the single-release answer); a reader applying held-for-sale accounting from outside the bundle might still reach 1,274. Recall: not a headline figure of a public law.
- Selected-lever checks: scatter the pieces: the amount (Doc 3) and its classification (Doc 5) sit in different releases. Lure recomputed: largest charge Doc 3 calls an impairment = 960 (notes/calc-i01-i02.py).
- Targeted failure modes: declared Linking across documents / Picks the wrong entity or section -> 960 (Doc 3 L514 Asset Impairments section and the three highlight mentions, L43, L147, L177; the $1,274 million sits at L528 under Transaction Gains/Losses). Not declared: 1,218 (net of the 2026 changes) and category totals (1,014, 1,045, 1,110), which the sentence's "recorded in fiscal 2025" and "single" rule out and no screen solver took.
- Calculation verification: no arithmetic beyond the comparison and the consistency check 66 - 56 = 10 (Doc 5) against Doc 4's printed $10 million; notes/calc-i01-i02.py asserts the Asset Impairments items sum to Doc 3's 1,110 (FY, pre-tax) and 1,014 (Q4) and computes the maximum. Units $ millions, pre-tax charges as printed.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: "impair" across all five texts (every hit listed in notes/doc-map.md); "held for sale"; "Africa"; "CCBA"; "1,274". Doc 3's own text never calls the 1,274 an impairment; the bundle overview for Doc 3 mentions only the "$960 million BODYARMOR impairment charge" (navigation only).
- Precision/readings: (a) impairments only as the 2025 releases label them -> 960; rejected by "Judging by Coca-Cola's earnings releases together" with Doc 5 L500. (b) the African impairment net of its 2026 changes -> 1,218 (1,274 + 10 - 66); rejected by "recorded in fiscal 2025". (c) a category total -> 1,014, 1,045 or 1,110; rejected by "single". (d) Nigeria 393 or Ghana as held-for-sale write-downs: smaller than 960 and 1,274 either way. (e) Whether all of the 1,274 is the impairment or only part (one screen solver's gap note): Doc 3 books it as one charge and Doc 5 calls the earlier charge "the previously recorded impairment charge"; the gold uses the charge as printed. Fiscal 2025 ends December 31, 2025.
- Completeness: capture complete (5 of 5 documents, no gap characters); Asset Impairments and Transaction Gains/Losses sections read in full in all five releases.
- Style/set review: one ask, 23 words. Sibling q02 uses Doc 1 and Doc 5's EPS outlooks; no shared facts, answer paths or wording.
- Warnings answered: pending the preflight.

sections.question: Judging by Coca-Cola's earnings releases together, what was the largest single impairment charge the company recorded in fiscal 2025, in millions of dollars?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 3, Asset Impairments, three months and year ended December 31, 2025): the largest charge Doc 3 describes as an impairment is "a charge of $960 million related to the impairment of our BODYARMOR trademark"; each other 2025 impairment charge it lists is smaller.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 3, Transaction Gains/Losses, same period): Doc 3 also records "a charge of $1,274 million related to our bottling operations in Africa that became held for sale", without calling it an impairment.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 5, Transaction Gains/Losses, three and six months ended July 3, 2026): Doc 5 records "a reduction in the previously recorded impairment charge" related to the same African bottling operations held for sale. Its second-quarter reduction is larger than its six-month reduction, so the first quarter of 2026 had added to that charge, and the second-quarter reduction is larger than that addition. The impairment charge being reduced therefore includes a charge recorded before 2026.
Step 4. Inference (Doc 3 and Doc 5): Doc 3's $1,274 million charge is the charge recorded on those same operations when they became held for sale, before 2026. Read together, the releases treat it as an impairment charge.
Step 5. Comparison (Doc 3 and Doc 5): $1,274 million is larger than the $960 million BODYARMOR impairment, so the largest single impairment charge recorded in fiscal 2025 is 1,274 million dollars. Doc 5's reductions were recorded in 2026 and do not change the fiscal 2025 amount.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

Why these are traps: Linking: Doc 3 books a $1,274 million charge on its African bottling operations held for sale under Transaction Gains/Losses, never calling it an impairment; its impairment section peaks at $960 million (BODYARMOR), the wrong answer. Doc 5 reduces "the previously recorded impairment charge" on those operations, so 1,274.
